A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph conformal prediction study despite the changed title and organization. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V1 reports original node-classification benchmarks, randomization and diffusion comparisons, NAPS sensitivity analyses, and CFGNN runtime experiments, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmarking, sensitivity, and runtime results in the main text and appendices, alongside revised overview results.

M1.justification: DTPS, randomized-APS CFGNN, batching and caching, and sparse batched NAPS already appear in v1. V2 reorganizes and expands their descriptions without establishing changes to their procedures or losses; the NAPS weighting formulas restate the existing neighborhood restriction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same transductive node-classification datasets, including ogbn-products and the Cora_ML comparison. The newly discussed inductive, dynamic-graph, and link-prediction settings are not newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds non-randomized APS to the overall alpha-sweep comparisons in Figures 7 and E5, corresponding to v1 Figures 6 and 16. APS already appeared in separate experiments, but its membership in these comparisons is new. The other comparator families and NAPS variants remain.

E3.justification: V2 removes the fixed two-layer, 128-hidden-unit CFGNN timing setting, described with 20 mini-batch epochs in v1. It retains the tuned-architecture, 50-epoch setting already reported in v1's appendix. The principal split schemes and tuning grids remain unchanged. V2's added label-stratified coverage formula conflicts with its verbal definition, so it does not establish an implemented metric change.

E4.justification: The fixed-architecture batching/caching control in v1 Table 7 is removed, reducing the scalability analysis. The tuned-architecture ablation survives in v2 Table C1, and the randomization, DTPS-versus-DAPS, and NAPS hop-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The retained CFGNN runtime and efficiency comparisons still report five trials and 95% confidence intervals. Boxplots and confidence bands also persist; no new seed counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: The overview adds non-randomized APS results and revises NAPS values. For example, Cora's exponential-NAPS set size at alpha = 0.1 under the stated FS, k = 5 setting changes from approximately 16.7 to 14.9 in Figure 16 versus Figure E5. Fixed-architecture timing entries disappear, while the tuned runtime and efficiency values from v1 Tables 8–9 remain unchanged in v2 Table C1.

T1.justification: The sufficient-condition theorem is retained as Theorem 2.3, but Appendix B substantially revises its foundation: uniformly sampled incorrect labels replace arbitrary incorrect labels, an exchangeability argument and Lemmas B.1–B.2 are added, and incorrect-label miscoverage becomes explicitly computable. V2 also adds Corollary 2.3.1 and its asymptotic proof, and qualifies Theorem 2.1's upper bound with a distinct-score or random tie-breaking assumption.

C1.justification: The benchmarking and scalability contributions remain. V2 explicitly presents efficiency comparison before deployment as a contribution and adds the asymptotic efficiency-gain claim. Its Section 3.5 summary also strengthens the randomization claim to 'provably more efficient,' although the theorem states a sufficient condition.

C2.justification: V2 newly warns that label-count sampling is biased and may violate exchangeability. It adds explicit method-selection guidance based on computational resources and adaptability, and interprets RAPS's benefits as less evident for transductive node classification. The inductive-setting limitation and label-imbalance explanations largely existed in v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit code-repository link and states that experiment configurations and best-model architectures are available there. V1 mentioned the library without providing that access information. Hardware, hyperparameter search spaces, and ogbn-products batching and neighbor-sampling details are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix F extends positioning to conformal link prediction, dynamic graphs, and non-conformal uncertainty calibration. Additional citations include Vadlamani et al. for the theoretical construction and newer graph conformal work. These contextual extensions preserve the central positioning around transductive node-classification benchmarks.

P1.justification: V2 substantially restructures the narrative: method descriptions are consolidated in Section 2.2, theory precedes experiments, explicit contributions and research questions are introduced, and Section 3.5 provides extended insights and guidelines. Appendix methods are reordered, CFGNN material moves from Appendix E to C, and a related-work appendix is added.

P2.justification: The overview line plots become grouped bar charts with coverage-reference lines and revised legends. Figure 1 expands using previously reported ogbn-arxiv evidence, and its label distribution is brought into the main text. Runtime and efficiency tables are combined and relocated, several panels are rearranged, and the document adopts a substantially different visual format.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves exposition and reproducibility through clearer method organization, explicit incorrect-label reasoning, the LC exchangeability warning, and code/configuration access. Most empirical evidence was already present, and the fixed-architecture timing control is lost. The inconsistent new label-stratified coverage formula and unconditional APS-superiority wording despite a conditional theorem limit the gains, supporting a modest overall improvement.
